applicant_utility.summary: There is no scholarship form to fill in: submitting your application to an English-taught Padua degree programme through apply.unipd.it is what puts you into the competition, so your real deadline is that programme's admission deadline (the first call for 2027/28 runs 15 September - 15 November 2026). The award pays EUR 8,000 gross per year in two EUR 4,000 instalments plus a tuition fee-waiver, but you still pay the regional tax and revenue stamp, and travel, insurance and other expenses are explicitly excluded. Timing decides whether you ever see the first instalment: it is credited only on arrival in Padua, and not at all if you arrive after 15 December (30 November for awards funded by the Civil, Environmental and Architectural Engineering department). Keeping the money in later years is a credits race - 12 ECTS by end of March 2027 for the second instalment, 40 by end of September 2027 and 60 by end of March 2028 for renewal - and falling below 20 ECTS by 30 November 2027 means revocation and repayment of what you already received.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong-track-record international applicants to English-taught Padova programmes who can commit to arriving before mid-December and sustaining a high credit pace from the first exam session
application_readiness_checklist: Open the Admission Notice or factsheet of your chosen English-taught programme and note its own deadlines, not the generic scholarship dates
Prepare the entry qualification (12-year school record for Bachelor's, foreign Bachelor's for Master's) plus passport and documents per the apply.unipd.it document list before the window opens
Pay the application fee and submit within the programme's first period, since awards in the second period are exceptional
Sort out an Italian or SEPA IBAN (own or joint account, prepaid card, or upgraded University Flash Card) before enrolment
Plan travel so you land in Padua well before 15 December (30 November if your award is DICEA-funded)
Build your first-year exam timetable around 12 ECTS by end of March and 40 ECTS by end of September
common_rejection_risks: Being treated as resident in Italy: EU citizens continuously resident for more than 9 months, or non-EU holders of a valid enrolment residence permit, are excluded even if they otherwise qualify
Holding Italian citizenship without qualifying dual citizenship
Applying only in the second application period, when scholarships are awarded on an exceptional basis
Missing the programme's admission deadline because you assumed a separate, later scholarship deadline existed
Failing to obtain the entry qualification by the deadline in the admission offer
Holding or accepting another public scholarship or grant, which makes the award incompatible
Arriving after the instalment cut-off, so the first EUR 4,000 is never credited
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The regional tax for the right to education and the revenue stamp payable every academic year; flights to Italy and any travel; health insurance; accommodation and general living costs beyond the EUR 8,000 annual allowance; the Italian student visa; the application and admission fees
document_audit: The entry qualification undergoes authenticity checks, and enrolment is finalised only after them, so allow time for legalisation or CIMEA statements if required
The IBAN must belong to you (or be jointly held); a parent's or third-party account breaks the payment step
Dual-citizenship status must be evidenced if you hold both Italian and another citizenship
The Declaration of acceptance must be signed, and any incompatibility with other scholarships promptly notified to international.admission@unipd.it
alerts: The 2027/2028 first call closes on 15 November 2026 and the scholarship-specific call is expected in November 2026 - do not wait for it before applying
If you transfer to another university or withdraw, you must repay the instalments already received
Credits earned before enrolment (recognised prior learning) never count towards the maintenance milestones
The arrival cut-off is stricter (30 November 2026) only for awards funded by the Department of Civil, Environmental and Architectural Engineering
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online application per chosen programme at apply.unipd.it within its call, then the programme's Academic Committee ranks eligible applicants, the Global Engagement Office emails successful candidates a scholarship offer to accept alongside the admission offer, and payment follows enrolment, IBAN registration and arrival in Padua

The scholarship is worth EUR 8,500 per year for female students enrolled in STEM programmes and EUR 7,200 per year in all other cases, and holders are exempted from paying tuition fees for that year. It is paid in two instalments, the second conditional on the credits earned in the January and February exam sessions, and it lasts a maximum of two years on a master's programme and three years on an undergraduate programme.

applicant_utility.summary: Do not look for a scholarship form: the money rides on your application to a Trento degree programme through the annual call for non-European candidates living abroad, published on each programme's own website with applications open between December and March. The award is EUR 7,200 per year, or EUR 8,500 if you are a female student on a STEM programme, plus exemption from that year's tuition fees, and it is paid in two instalments. The second instalment is the trap: it is only paid in May if you have already banked at least 50% of your course credits in the January and February exam sessions, otherwise you wait until October and need 42 credits (36 on Italian-taught courses) by 10 August. Every September the University re-checks your 10 August credits; miss the target and you hand part of the scholarship back and pay next year's tuition in full.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU citizens living abroad with strong academic records, especially women applying to STEM programmes (the EUR 8,500 tier), who can hit the December-March window and front-load credits in their first exam sessions
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you genuinely qualify as a non-European citizen residing abroad - EU citizens and non-EU residents of Italy cannot use this route
Find your programme's own call on its website (corsi.unitn.it) rather than a central portal, and diarise its exact deadline and 12:00 CET cut-off
Pay the EUR 30.00 application fee and upload the passport, degree certificate and transcript with official translations where they are not in English or Italian
Line up English evidence that matches one of the accepted formats: certificate, university statement that the degree was taught in English, or self-declaration from an English-speaking country
After admission, plan Universitaly pre-enrolment within two weeks of confirmation and the type-D visa before enrolment
Register for January and February exams early in the year so the 50% credit condition for the second instalment is realistic
common_rejection_risks: Assuming a separate scholarship application exists and missing the programme admission deadline entirely
Citizenship or residence mismatch: being an EU citizen, or living in Italy, disqualifies you from this award even with excellent grades
Ranking below the limited number of scholarships, since assignation depends purely on the admission score
Uploading untranslated or illegible documents, which the calls explicitly exclude from the selection
Losing the second instalment by underperforming in the January and February sessions
Failing to obtain the Bachelor's degree by 30 June (non-Europeans graduating abroad) or 31 October, which breaks the enrolment chain
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Rent for on-campus accommodation (guaranteed for admitted non-European students but at a rent); registration with the Italian National Health Service and insurance; flights and travel; the EUR 30.00 application fee; and, if credit targets are missed, next year's tuition of EUR 1,000 to EUR 10,000 depending on the programme's maximum fee band and the credits actually earned
document_audit: Every document not in English or Italian needs an official translation; the call warns that illegible or incomplete applications are excluded
The passport must stay valid through the visa and pre-enrolment stages
The transcript must show examinations, results and credits - a bare degree certificate is not enough
English-language proof must fit one of the three accepted formats; an unrelated test score or an ambiguous statement can stall the admission file
alerts: For 2027/2028 entry the call is expected around December 2026 - the 2026/2027 window closed on 4 March 2026, so there is a long closed season to plan around
Scholarship confirmation is re-verified every September against the credits you hold by 10 August, so year two is never guaranteed
If you fall short you must return part of the scholarship and pay full tuition for the following year according to the published credit-fee tables
The higher EUR 8,500 tier applies only to female students enrolled in STEM programmes - check which tier your programme and profile fall into before budgeting
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Programme-level online application published on each course site, ranking list with admitted candidates and scholarship assignation, confirmation of the place by the deadline UniTrento communicates, Universitaly pre-enrolment, visa, then enrolment in Trento with instalments arriving in December and May
